scenes.headline: How a giant hash table feeds a language model
scenes.sub: Tinfield 1, and the engram table inside its Qwen base.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Nutmeg! Tinfield 1 carries a fifty-one-billion-parameter hash table. A token barely touches it.

scenes.label: What's in the download
scenes.text: Tinfield 1 is Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with its attention retrained: 1.85% of the weights moved. The biggest single piece is a hashed n-gram table.
scenes.say: Tinfield 1 is Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with retrained attention: one point eight five percent of the weights. Its biggest piece is a hashed n-gram table.

scenes.title: Where the change is, and where the table plugs in

steps.say: A token climbs forty-eight layers of attention and a mixture of five hundred and twelve experts.
The fine-tune moved every attention projection, and nothing else.

steps.note: byte for byte the base model
steps.say: All five hundred and twelve experts, in every layer, are byte for byte the base model.
At layer two, one extra input arrives from the engram table: Qwen's, and also unchanged.
Take the last two or three token ids, and hash them with three large multipliers.
Reduce it modulo sixteen different primes, each just above twenty million: sixteen unrelated collision patterns.
Each head picks a row of a hundred and sixty numbers from its own slice.
The sixteen rows are concatenated, and gated into the residual stream at layer two.

scenes.title: Why sixteen primes and not one table

left.title: One huge table
items: Two n-grams that collide stay confused, permanently
Nothing to average the collision away
left.say: With one huge table, two n-grams on the same row are confused forever.

right.title: Sixteen prime-sized heads
items: A collision under one prime almost never repeats under another
Concatenating sixteen rows averages the noise out
right.say: With sixteen prime-sized heads, a collision under one prime almost never repeats, so the noise averages out.

scenes.label: values a token reads, out of 51.2 billion in the table
scenes.note: a gather of about 5 KB, with no matrix multiply attached
scenes.say: A token reads two thousand five hundred and sixty values out of fifty-one billion: about five kilobytes, no matrix multiply.

scenes.title: The release's only chart
scenes.credit: needmorevramog's own chart, mirrored in the badtheorylabs org

steps.say: The release's only chart is mirrored from a quantizer: a check of one quantized build.
Perplexity rises zero point four two percent, against its own source quant, not the full weights.

scenes.text: Embeddings scale by lookup, not by matmul. That is why the 26.8 GiB table can stay memory-mapped on the CPU.
scenes.say: So embeddings scale by lookup, not matrix multiply. That's why the table can stay memory-mapped on the CPU side.

recap: Tinfield 1 retrained attention: 1.85% of the weights
The engram table is a hashed n-gram embedding
Sixteen prime moduli average collisions away
scenes.say: To recap: retrained attention, and a hashed n-gram table read through sixteen primes.
